evidence:
Overall the 2 gate, 43 functional, 5 polish and 5 visual criteria are strongly outcome-based: nearly every binary row names a concrete browser observable (stage/place of a named probe card, refusal plus unchanged re-read, document.activeElement, getBoundingClientRect().top, unread count deltas within 15 s without reload, 401 status on a fresh-context replay, restart_app followed by fresh sign-in), uses distinctive per-review probes (suffixed J1/J2 jobs, cards A-F and V-Z/A2, distinctive draft text such as 'Call back on Fri'), and pairs refusals with positive controls. The stale-move protocol C deliberately uses an A-B-A sequence (F Applied->Screen, Mei Screen->Applied, replay Applied->Screen) so a stage-compare app cannot pass and only a real version check is credited - a well-designed distinctive probe. Visual rows are likert with five described anchors (visual/judge.toml:17-90); they are craft judgements, not 'looks right' binaries, so they are acceptable here (Note only). Gates (render/judge.toml:22-24, constraints/judge.toml:22-24) require a real create plus independent-context readback, excluding static shells.

Instances that are not cleanly browser-decidable (reported per the row's 'every instance' wording):

(1) hro_candidate_private (functional/judge.toml:386-390, weight 2.5) says 'no response a candidate page receives contains internal notes, a rejection reason, a rejected-from stage, board positions ...', and protocol K (functional/prompt.md:43) says 'Capture every request the candidate page makes and inspect every response'. Neither tells the judge how to observe server-sent-event or WebSocket payloads, which rules section 5 explicitly allows ('Polling, server-sent events and sockets are all acceptable', hireops_rules.md:123). Playwright MCP network listings do not expose event-stream bodies, and response.body() on a text/event-stream does not resolve while the stream is open. The leak is therefore not reliably observable on the most likely leak channel, while K itself rejects and reopens Tomas's card during the candidate session - exactly when a broadcast would carry the reason.

(2) hro_stale_refused (functional/judge.toml:194-201, weight 2.5, the heaviest functional row together with hro_live_board/hro_candidate_private): the 'who' leg is decided on a page.evaluate replay ('the refusal says the card was changed and names who changed it (in the response or on screen)', prompt.md:33). A replay through fetch never reaches the app's UI, so only the response body can carry the name. The public requirement is UI-level ('tell me who', instruction.md:3; 'The person is told that the card was changed and by whom', hireops_rules.md:79-80). The golden passes because its 409 message embeds the latest activity detail (src/index.js:242-244), and the scripted golden proves the on-screen variant only after aborting /api/events (workspace.cjs:272-278), a technique the judge prompt does not offer. An app whose 409 body carries only an actor id that its UI resolves to 'Mei Lin' is graded as failing the 'names who' leg although it satisfies the brief.

(3) hro_pol_live_board (polish/judge.toml:17-24, weight 3 of 12 polish): 'scroll the page, or the board's scroll container if the page itself does not scroll, so it is not at the top ... the scroll position has not been reset ... Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.' The polish protocol builds a job with only three cards (polish/prompt.md:16). A conforming compact desktop app whose page and board both fit the viewport has nothing to scroll; the criterion defines no outcome for that case, so a strict judge can zero a correct app on an unsatisfiable setup leg (a lenient judge passes it vacuously) - an undecidable leg, not an outcome.

No source-read, 'looks right' binary, or no-trace probe was found elsewhere. Runtime evidence: the scripted golden run (raw-evidence-index, hashes verified) covers the golden only; no configured judge run, weak-app run or Oracle exists, so none of the three instances is CONFIRMED or REFUTED by a measured judge run.
counterexample: (a) Plausible broken app that could pass: an Express app that pushes every board event over one SSE channel to all signed-in clients, e.g. data: {"type":"move","card":{"candidate_name":"Tomas Varga","stage":"REJECTED","rejection_reason":"<reason>","rejected_from":"SCREEN","position":2}}, while its REST reads for candidates are correctly filtered. During protocol K the judge inspects captured REST responses (all clean), cannot read the open event stream, and awards hro_candidate_private 2.5 although the candidate's browser received a rejection reason. (b) Conforming alternative that could fail: an app whose 409 stale body is {"error":"stale","changed_by":"U-mei","version":7} and whose UI renders 'Mei Lin moved this card a moment ago' from its user list; the judge's fetch replay shows no name, nothing appears on screen, and hro_stale_refused (2.5) scores 0. (c) Conforming alternative that could fail: a board-only desktop layout with job/candidate forms in dialogs, where a three-card job fits the 1280x720 viewport with no vertical page or board scroll; the 'scroll ... so it is not at the top' leg cannot be performed and hro_pol_live_board (3/12 of polish) may be scored 0 despite perfect preservation of the open card, note text and focus.
suggested_fix: (1) In hro_candidate_private/protocol K, tell the judge that when the candidate page uses an event stream or socket observed in the network log, it reads that stream in the candidate's session (e.g. page.evaluate with new EventSource(observedUrl) or page.on('websocket') framereceived) throughout the reject/reopen of Tomas's card and counts its payloads as received responses. (2) In hro_stale_refused, accept the person identified either by name in the response or on screen, or by an identifier that the app's own observed staff data maps to that person, (or obtain the UI message by an allowed stale attempt). (3) In hro_pol_live_board, add: 'if neither the page nor the board scrolls at this viewport, add cards until one does, or record that no scroll exists and judge the remaining legs.'
